chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be made your ransom! I used to recite the Quran but it has escaped from me, so supplicate to God, Mighty and Majestic, that He teach it to me.' He (the narrator) said: It was as if he (the Imam) was alarmed at that, and he said: 'May God teach it to you and to us all.' He said: 'And we were approximately ten.'

Then he said: 'The surah is with the man who had recited it and then abandoned it. It will come to him on the Day of Resurrection in the most beautiful form, and will greet him. He will say: Who are you? It will say: I am such-and-such surah. Had you adhered to me and held fast to me, I would have brought you down to this rank. Therefore, it is upon you to (adhere to) the Quran.'

Then he said: 'Among the people is one who recites the Quran so that it be said, so-and-so is a reciter; and among them is one who recites the Quran to seek worldly gains through it, and there is no goodness in that; and among them is one who recites the Quran to benefit from it in his salat, his night, and his day.'

key_terms.الدَّرَجَةَ: The rank/station in paradise — the spiritual reward that could have been earned
key_terms.فَزِعَ: Was alarmed/shocked — indicating the gravity the Imam attached to forgetting the Quran
key_terms.فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالْقُرْآنِ: It is upon you to adhere to the Quran — a formulaic exhortation
key_terms.فَفَلَتَ مِنِّي: It escaped/slipped from me — an idiom for forgetting memorized Quran

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about forgetting the Quran after memorizing it?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a companion who had forgotten the Quran he once memorized with a dramatic vision: the forgotten surah will appear in the most beautiful form on the Day of Resurrection, lamenting that the man's neglect cost him a lofty rank in paradise. The Imam then categorizes Quran reciters into three types — those seeking reputation, those seeking worldly gain, and those who recite for spiritual benefit — condemning the first two and praising only sincere recitation integrated into daily worship. This teaching was addressed to a group of approximately ten companions, making it a public exhortation on the purpose and etiquette of Quran recitation.
